sources.entry: Prometheus | Monitoring system and time series database

summary.one_liner: Prometheus is an open-source systems and service monitoring system and time series database that collects metrics from configured targets, evaluates rules, graphs results, and triggers alerts.
summary.what_it_does: Prometheus collects metrics from configured targets at set intervals and stores them as multi-dimensional time series, identified by metric name and key/value labels. It evaluates rule expressions and can trigger alerts when specified conditions are met. Users query the data with PromQL and view results through graphing and dashboarding modes. Targets are found through service discovery or static configuration, and it supports federation across servers. Batch jobs can push metrics through an intermediary gateway. The README describes it as a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
use_cases: collect and store time series metrics
monitor batch jobs via a push gateway
stack: Docker images on Quay.io and Docker Hub
notable: Multi-dimensional data model with PromQL query language
Single server nodes are autonomous, with no distributed storage dependency
Pull-based HTTP collection with service discovery or static config
Optional service discovery plugins can be excluded at build time with Go build tags
Remote Write protobuf published separately on buf.build
caveats: Not designed as a Go library; the README warns of errors that surface only when used as a library
Building from source requires Go, Node.js, and npm 10 or greater
Out-of-tree plugins are not endorsed and may need go.mod and go.sum changes
keywords: get alerts when server metrics spike
